function: above_phy: a Decision Transformer learns the AAV trajectory and user scheduling (AAV-user association) to minimize average AoI (p. 1, p. 3); transmit power and bandwidth are fixed (p. 4).
notes: Step 1 exclusion, code above_phy. The method is learned (a Decision Transformer pre-trained with supervised learning on expert trajectories, p. 3), so no_learning does not apply; above_phy is the first code that does. The learned decisions are the UAV trajectory and user scheduling/association, which the instructions list as above the physical layer. p. 1: "framework to optimize trajectory planning and user scheduling"; p. 2: "jointly optimizing the AAV’s trajectory Q ... and the user selection"; p. 3: "The AAV agent’s action at time slot t consists of the AAV’s flight distance, flight angle, and the AAV-user association". No learned physical-layer decision on the aerial link (no transmit power, resource, or beam control) that would let it pass jointly: p. 4: "Each user uploads a task of size Nu = 30 Mb with a power of Pu = 0.5 W. The channel bandwidth is B = 1 MHz". The per-slot uplink (hovering) time, delta_h = delta - delta_f (p. 2), is a by-product of the learned flight distance and not a decision variable of problem P1, which optimizes only the trajectory Q and the user selection (p. 2); the reviewer may confirm this reading. The abstract's "dynamic resource allocation" (p. 1) describes earlier DT work, not this paper's decision. Title and DOI 10.1109/LWC.2025.3575757 confirmed on p. 1.
